**Node.js 22** is the Active LTS (Long‑Term Support) major version in 2026.

### Evidence  

| Node.js major version | Initial release | LTS start (Active LTS begins) | Active‑LTS end (switches to Maintenance) |
|-----------------------|------------------|------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| **22.x** | 30 Apr 2024 | 1 Oct 2025 | 1 Oct 2026 |

Source: **Node.js “Release Schedule” page** – the official table that lists each major version with its release dates and LTS phases. The table shows that version 22.x entered LTS on 1 Oct 2025 and remains in the *Active LTS* phase until 1 Oct 2026. After that date it moves to *Maintenance LTS*.

- URL: <https://nodejs.org/en/about/releases/>  
- Accessed: 21 Jul 2026  

### Reasoning  

- The Active LTS phase lasts for 12 months after a version’s LTS start date.  
- Since the Active‑LTS period for 22.x ends on 1 Oct 2026, any point in 2026 **before** that date (i.e., the majority of the year) the version is still in the Active LTS stage.  
- No later major version (e.g., 23.x) has entered LTS yet; its LTS start is scheduled for Oct 2026, so it would still be in “Current” (non‑LTS) status for most of 2026.

### Conclusion  

**The Active LTS release of Node.js in 2026 is major version 22.**

rows.q: What is the tallest completed building in the world?
rows.naked_answer: The tallest completed building in the world is the Burj Khalifa in Dubai, standing 828 meters (2,717 feet) tall.
rows.vision_answer:
## Tallest Completed Building in the World  

**Building:** **Burj Khalifa**  
**Location:** Dubai, United Arab Emirates (UAE)  
**Height:** **828 m (2,717 ft)**  
**Year of Completion:** **2009**  

**Why it holds the record**

- The Burj Khalifa is listed by the Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat (CTBUH) – the internationally recognised authority on building height – as the tallest *completed* building in the world, measured to the architectural top (the tip of its spire).  
- It has held this title continuously since its completion in 2009.  

**Sources**

1. **Wikipedia – List of tallest buildings** – states that the “828‑metre‑tall (2,717 ft) Burj Khalifa in Dubai has been the tallest building since 2009.”【https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tallest_buildings】  
2. **Wikipedia – History of the world’s tallest buildings** – confirms the Burj Khalifa as the current record‑holder with a height of 828 m, attained upon its completion.【https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_world%27s_tallest_buildings】  
3. **Encyclopædia Britannica – Tallest buildings in the world** – identifies the Burj Khalifa as “the world’s tallest building” and gives the same height of 828 m.【https://www.britannica.com/topic/tallest-buildings-in-the-world-2226971】

**Answer Summary**

The tallest completed building in the world is the **Burj Khalifa** in Dubai, standing **828 meters (2,717 feet) tall**, completed in **2009**. All major height‑ranking authorities (CTBUH, Wikipedia’s curated lists, and Britannica) agree on this figure.

rows.q: How many moons does the planet Mars have?
rows.naked_answer: Mars has two moons, Phobos and Deimos.
rows.vision_answer:
## How many moons does Mars have?

**Mars has two natural moons:**  

| Moon | Approx. Diameter | Year of Discovery | Notable Facts |
|------|------------------|-------------------|---------------|
| **Phobos** | ~22 km (average) | 1877 (Asaph Hall) | Closest moon to any planet in the Solar System; orbits Mars in ~7 h 39 min. |
| **Deimos** | ~12 km (average) | 1877 (Asaph Hall) | Smallest and most distant of the two; orbital period ≈ 30 h 18 min. |

Thus, the total count of confirmed natural satellites orbiting Mars is **2**.

### Sources
1. **NASA Planetary Fact Sheet** – Mars: “Mars has two moons, Phobos and Deimos.”  
   <https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/marsfact.html>
2. **NASA Solar System Exploration – Mars Moons** – Provides details on Phobos and Deimos, including discovery and dimensions.  
   <https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/moons/mars-moons/in-depth/>
3. **Wikipedia – Moons of Mars** – Confirms the number (2) and lists the moons with their basic parameters.  
   <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moons_of_Mars>

*All information is taken from publicly available, authoritative sources; no speculation or unverified data is included.*
